decision.scope: Add the H3 secret-boundary and evidence-ladder atoms only to an explicit private registry and static evaluator boundary; keep the default compiler on H2.

hypothesis.predicted_direction: Pairing explicit evidence authority with a complete quality ladder separates security blockers from release unknowns.
hypothesis.falsifier: An unowned sensitive boundary or incomplete quality ladder is admitted without a stop.

valid_arms.predicted_delta: Release evidence containing sensitive material cannot satisfy the ladder until its owner and handling scope are recorded.
Security readiness distinguishes complete, partial, blocked, and unknown verification instead of treating one green check as sufficient.

acceptance_gates: H3 activation requires atom-specific semantic signals and cannot be activated by lexical candidates.
The two H3 atoms preserve their H2 typed dependencies and fail closed when those dependencies are absent.
Frozen positive, negative, and ambiguous fixtures pass at the private static boundary.
H3 cannot render to packet or receipt targets.
The default H2 registry, H1/H2 projections, public contracts, routing, admission, and provider behavior remain unchanged.
stop_conditions: A family-level signal implicitly activates H3 through the default compiler.
A secret-boundary finding proceeds without explicit authority and boundary evidence.
A partial or stale quality ladder is represented as complete.
H3 reaches a public packet, receipt, provider cell, cross-skill composition, admission, or routing boundary.
